_what_this_is: The working recipe behind scripts/demo/record-demo.mjs, which regenerates docs/demo.gif (the animated demo in README.md). To reshoot it: `npm run build` then `npm run demo:record`.
prereqs: npm run build  — dist/card.js must be current; the recorder loads that exact bundle, not src/
ffmpeg on PATH — two-pass palette GIF encode
npx playwright install chromium — once per machine; `playwright` is a devDependency
hard_constraints: The recorder only navigates its own standalone rig, scripts/demo/record-harness.html. It never writes to src/, dist/ (rebuild with `npm run build`), or any docs/ file other than the output gif.
scripts/demo/record-harness.html is committed so the recipe is reproducible without rebuilding the rig from scratch. It is NOT a user-facing page.

card_setConfig.pinned: DOW JONES, S&P 500, NASDAQ, FTSE 100, Nikkei 225, Gold, Crude Oil, USD/PLN, USD/JPY, DAX, VIX — rendered in configured order, never sorted
card_setConfig.sorted: Apple, Microsoft, NVidia (mark: gold), Tesla (icon: ★), Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Bitcoin, AMD, Netflix, JPMorgan — ranked by regularMarketChangePercent descending

harness_config.fake_data: One state object per sensor.yahoofinance_<slug> entity, shaped like the real YahooFinanceAttributes (src/types.ts). Indices/commodities/FX pairs legitimately omit PE/dividend/volume, same as real sensor data. No real Home Assistant, no WebSocket: the harness gives the card a connection object with no subscribeEvents, so the card re-renders on every `card.hass = …` assignment (SubscriptionManager bails out early). The same connection object is reused across assignments so the card never treats it as a reconnect.
harness_config.mount_order: createElement → setConfig → appendChild → set .hass. setConfig before connecting matters for the same reason it does elsewhere in this card family.
harness_config.recorder_hook: window.__tick(i) applies TICKS[i - 1] (a partial patch keyed by entity id, defined in the harness) and re-assigns .hass. Four scripted ticks drift prices/rates across a mix of pinned and sorted rows; tick 2 spikes AAPL past NVDA (re-sorting the sorted section) and flips USD/PLN's marketState from PRE to REGULAR (its price source, prepost background, and name color switch together); tick 4 spikes NVDA back past AAPL (re-sorts again).

recorder.capture_method: Real page.screenshot() with a fixed clip, sampled in a sleep/hold loop. Motion in the gif is the card's own JS (data-column rotation timer, the re-sort, the market-state recolor) sampled continuously — nothing is synthesized.
recorder.clip: measured once from #wrap's bounding box after window.__ready, reused for every frame; width/height floored to even numbers for the encoder (flooring, not rounding — rounding up can catch a 1px sliver of page background below the card and it reads as a dark line)
recorder.encode: ffmpeg two-pass palette (palettegen max_colors=128 stats_mode=diff, paletteuse dither=bayer) scaled to 460px wide (1x — the box's CSS width). Height comes entirely from how many pinned/sorted rows the harness configures, not from output scaling.

scenario_beats: tick 1 — modest drift across DOW JONES, Gold, Apple, NVidia (prices and 1d% shift, no re-sort yet). hold ~1.5s
tick 2 — AAPL's 1d% jumps past NVDA's, re-sorting the sorted section; USD/PLN flips PRE → REGULAR, switching its price source and colors together; S&P 500 drifts. hold ~1.5s
tick 3 — Tesla drops further, Meta slides, Bitcoin jumps. hold ~1.5s
tick 4 — NVDA spikes back past AAPL (re-sorts again), AMD flips from red to green, VIX spikes. hold ~1.5s
hold ~1s of resting frames before the gif loops
known_risks: HACS renders a repo's README from its latest release tag, not from main. Merging a demo.gif change to main does not update what HACS users see until a new version is tagged. The README badge points at raw.githubusercontent.com/…/main/…, which is not tag-pinned and updates on every push.

data_rotate_every and the hold-frame counts are tuned together — if data_rotate_every changes, retune the hold(N) calls in record-demo.mjs's runScenario() so each column change still lands mid-hold, not at a cut.
